clauses.quote: 1.4 Emergency medical condition. A medical condition with acute symptoms of sufficient severity, including severe pain, that a prudent layperson with an average knowledge of health and medicine could reasonably expect, without immediate medical attention, to place the health of the person in serious jeopardy or cause serious impairment of bodily functions.
clauses.why_it_helps: The member presented with sudden severe (8/10) right lower abdominal pain, fever, and tachycardia — acute symptoms of sufficient severity that a prudent layperson could reasonably expect to place health in serious jeopardy, so the visit qualifies as an emergency medical condition.

clauses.quote: 1.7 Medically necessary. Services that a treating clinician orders to diagnose or treat an illness, injury or its symptoms, consistent with generally accepted standards of medical practice, and not mainly for the convenience of the member or the clinician.
clauses.why_it_helps: The CT was ordered by the treating emergency clinician to diagnose the cause of acute abdominal pain with fever and leukocytosis, consistent with accepted practice — it was not for convenience — so it meets the plan's own definition of medically necessary, directly rebutting the CO-50 denial.

clauses.quote: 1.9 Emergency services. A medical screening examination in an emergency department and the further examination, imaging and treatment needed to stabilize the member.
clauses.why_it_helps: The CT is 'imaging' performed in the emergency department as part of the further examination needed after the screening exam, so it falls within the plan's definition of emergency services.

clauses.quote: 5.2 Emergency services. The plan covers emergency services for an emergency medical condition, including diagnostic imaging ordered by the treating emergency clinician, at the in-network cost-sharing level. The plan decides whether a visit was an emergency from the symptoms present when the member sought care, not from the final diagnosis. A claim for emergency services will not be denied solely because the final diagnosis was not an emergency.
clauses.why_it_helps: This is the strongest clause: it expressly covers diagnostic imaging ordered by the treating emergency clinician, and states the emergency determination is made from the presenting symptoms, not the final diagnosis — so the benign final diagnosis (mesenteric adenitis) cannot ground the CO-50 denial.

clauses.quote: 5.3 Advanced imaging. CT, MRI and PET scans performed outside an emergency department need prior authorization. Prior authorization is not required for imaging performed during an emergency department visit.
clauses.why_it_helps: The CT was performed during an emergency department visit, so no prior authorization was required — the plan cannot rely on a missing prior authorization as a basis for denial.

clauses.title: The plan's own words
clauses.text: The plan's own terms support coverage. The Plan Evidence of Coverage, section 5.2, page 2, says: "5.2 Emergency services. The plan covers emergency services for an emergency medical condition, including diagnostic imaging ordered by the treating emergency clinician, at the in-network cost-sharing level. The plan decides whether a visit was an emergency from the symptoms present when the member sought care, not from the final diagnosis. A claim for emergency services will not be denied solely because the final diagnosis was not an emergency." The enclosed records show: "Sudden severe right lower abdominal pain for 6 hours, pain 8 of 10, with nausea and one episode of vomiting." (ED record, page 1); "Temperature 38.6 C. Heart rate 112. Right lower quadrant tenderness with guarding and rebound." (ED record, page 1); "White blood cell count 15.2 (high)." (ED record, page 1). A published imaging guideline ("Imaging of the Abdomen and Pelvis 2025-03-23 [for Amerigroup Georgia Medicaid]", https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/imaging-of-the-abdomen-and-pelvis-2025-03-23/) lists as medically necessary: "Acute abdominal pain EITHER associated with clinical findings of a surgical abdomen, including severe undifferentiated abdominal pain or guarding, OR acute pain that remains unexplained after ALL of the following:" Its imaging study for this pain is "CT abdomen and/or pelvis for lower quadrant (right or left) and generalized abdominal pain". Please apply these terms to the denied service. Each quote above is copied from the document named, not paraphrased.
